title: Episodic prefetch conductor for mixed-length inference
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Introduce a lightweight 'episodic prefetch conductor' that reduces KV cache fragmentation and peak GPU memory by managing prefetch and reservation at the conversation/episode boundary instead of purely per-slot continuous admission. Targets mixed prompt/response workloads where short assistant turns interleave with long context passages, causing slot churn and suboptimal KV residency.
background: Continuous batching works well for throughput but mixed-length dialogues create fragmentation: long episodes pin KV entries while many short turns create high admission/eviction churn. Current slot coalescing reduces some churn but cannot easily enforce per-episode locality or guard against long-turn over-reservation. We need an orchestration layer to reason about episode-level prefetch windows, soft reservations, and compaction windows that cooperate with the slot allocator and KV GC.
proposal: Build a conductor that attaches ephemeral 'episode handles' to incoming requests. On episode start (first user message) the conductor optionally prefetches model KV pages predicted to be needed for the upcoming N turns using lightweight length forecasts. The conductor maintains a soft per-episode reservation (token-budget-based) and exposes a small set of runtime signals: reserve(kv_bytes), release(kv_bytes), fence(turn_boundary), compact(window_ms). The runtime honors reservations preferentially and performs compaction windows at low-utilization intervals. Prefetch is gated by a feature flag and controlled by per-instance budgets.
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces eviction rate for conversations, lowers tail latency for short assistant turns, enables more aggressive packing for throughput. Cons: increases orchestration complexity, may mis-forecast leading to wasted prefetched KV memory, introduces policy interactions with existing slot coalescing and autoscaling policies.
experiments: Experiment A: fixed-size per-episode reservation vs adaptive reservation using moving-average turn length; measure KV eviction rate and peak GPU memory
Experiment B: fence-based prefetch (prefetch at turn boundary only) vs continuous opportunistic prefetch; measure p95/p99 latency and CPU overhead
Experiment C: compaction window sizes (50ms, 200ms, 1s) to trade compaction cost vs reclaimed memory
metric_targets: p95 generation latency for short-turn workload <= 180ms (no regression vs baseline)
avg GPU memory utilization decrease 8-12% on mixed-trace replays
KV eviction rate reduction >= 30% on mixed traces
implementation_notes: High-level: conductor lives in scheduler layer, decision hot path implemented in C++ with a tiny control-plane state machine in Rust/Go for orchestration. Add per-episode metadata to request envelopes. Reuse existing metrics tags (slot_id, episode_id, model, instance_type). Expose knobs via runtime config: episode_prefetch_enable, episode_soft_quota_tokens, compaction_window_ms, fence_grace_ms. Ensure instrumentation emits reservation/grant/release events for offline analysis.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Feature-flagged conductor merged behind flag; 2) A/B in staging shows metric targets met for 2 weeks on replay and 48h live; 3) No >2% increase in error rate or >5% latency regressions for any traffic cohort; 4) Integration tests and regression suites covering streaming re-entrance, early-release, and forced-eviction scenarios added.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary in staging with 5% synthetic traffic using trace replayer; 2) Staging A/B with 10% production-like replay; 3) Gradual ramp to 25% on a dedicated small instance fleet with close telemetry; 4) Opt-in for selected customers on Dedicated; 5) Full enablement after 2 weeks of stability and postmortem review.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: over-reserving KV memory for long episodes -> Mitigation: adaptive decay and soft quotas with auto-release on inactivity
Risk: additional CPU overhead in orchestration -> Mitigation: offload decision path to fast-path C++ and amortize across slots
Risk: interactions with existing slot coalescing -> Mitigation: coordinate with slot allocator via new API contracts and add cross-check invariants
